question: Deimachus who was a Greek ambassador came to India during the reign of the Mauryan king, ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bindusara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Deimachus was a Greek ambassador who came to India during the reign of the Mauryan king Bindusara.
 
• Bindusara was the second Mauryan emperor, ruling from c. 297 to c. 273 BCE.
 
• He was the son of Chandragupta Maurya, the founder of the Maurya Dynasty.
 
• Bindusara maintained diplomatic relations with various Hellenistic states, including the Seleucid Empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bindusara**

 
 
• Bindusara, also known as Amitraghata, was the second emperor of the Mauryan dynasty.
 
• He succeeded his father, Chandragupta Maurya, and ruled from c. 297 BCE to c. 273 BCE.
 
• Bindusara is known for his administrative skills and the expansion of the Mauryan Empire.
 
• He maintained friendly relations with the Hellenistic kingdoms, which were established by the successors of Alexander the Great.
 
 
 
• **Deimachus**
 
 
• Deimachus was a Greek envoy sent by Antiochus I, the Seleucid king, to the Mauryan court.
 
• His visit to India is recorded as part of the diplomatic relations between the Mauryan Empire and the Hellenistic world.
 
• Deimachus succeeded Megasthenes, another Greek ambassador, at the Mauryan court.
 
 
 
• **Mauryan Empire**
 
 
• The Mauryan Empire was the first large-scale empire in India, founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 322 BCE.
 
• It is known for its significant achievements in political, military, and cultural fields.
 
• The empire reached its zenith under Ashoka the Great, who is renowned for his promotion of Buddhism and non-violence.
 
 
 
• **Diplomatic Relations**
 
 
• During the Mauryan period, diplomatic relations were established with several Hellenistic kingdoms, including the Seleucid Empire.
 
• These relations were crucial for trade, cultural exchange, and political alliances.
 
• Greek ambassadors like Megasthenes and Deimachus played a key role in these diplomatic efforts.
